mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.5% signals a highly accommodative monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity in the markets and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months indicates strengthening consumer demand, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when RSAFS has increased for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points in a single month signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of the instances when UNRATE increases by more than 0.5pp in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% year-over-year signals a contraction in the supply side of the economy, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the instances when INDPRO declines by more than 2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strengthening economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when HOUST increases and UNRATE decreases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) over three consecutive months signals a strengthening labor market, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when PAYEMS has increased for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% month-over-month signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as markets anticipate tighter monetary policy.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of the instances when CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in real GDP (GDPC1) and decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a robust economic expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when GDPC1 increases and UNRATE decreases.
